newsitem.title: USA: House votes for curbs on foreign population funds.
newsitem.headline: House votes for curbs on foreign population funds.

text.p: The House of Representatives Thursday approved a bill that would reimpose Reagan-era restrictions on U.S. international family planning aid.
The bill was sent to the Senate where its fate was uncertain.

The bill, proposed by New Jersey Republican Christopher Smith and approved by a vote of 231-194, would bar U.S. funding of population planning organisations that perform or advocate abortions, even if they use their own money to do so.
These restrictions were in effect during the administrations of Presidents Ronald Reagan and George Bush but were lifted by President Clinton.

The vote followed House approval, on a 220-209 vote, of an administration-backed resolution speeding up the start of disbursement of $385 million international family planning funds to March 1 from July 1.
Smith's bill would also advance disbursement of the money and additionally remove limits on month-by-month release of the money, but it faces an almost certain veto if it reaches Clinton's desk.
